newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty plummets on foreign profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty plummets on foreign profit-taking.

text.p: The zloty plunged to 1.31/0.73 percent from the parity rate from 2.44/2.27 percent at opening on large scale foreign profit-taking on Polish instruments to cover losses suffered on the Czech crown, dealers said.
The National Bank of Poland said it was comfortable with the zloty at 1.9 percent above the parity rate and would watch closely what the zloty's further moves would be.

"Foreigners are selling large amounts of Polish paper, probably to cover losses suffered in the Czech Republic. The central bank is checking rates on the market, but has not intervened yet," said Malgorzata Sawicka of Bank Handlowy SA.
At 0800 GMT, however, it crept slightly up again to 1.21/0.85 percent above the trading band centre and dealers' views were mixed on whether it would start falling again.
It was at 3.1950/2050 against the dollar and 1.8800/80 against the mark, against 3.1600/50 and 1.8530/65 respectively at the opening.

"It is hard to say if the zloty has already stabilised because there seem to be no fundamental reasons for the zloty sales, only psychological ones. I think one percent from parity may prove to be a level of stabilisation," said Witold Wozniak, forex dealer at Deutsche Bank in Warsaw.

"There might be some nervousness after the Czech crown fall and the zloty might be suffering slightly from that but I don't think the situation is serious because there is no news which would justify selling the zloty," said Charles Camen of Paribas Capital Markets in London.
